events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Grand Haven, boat: 3 (good).** This is the port I'd go to.
- **South Haven, boat: 2 (average).** This is the backup.
- **Muskegon, boat: 1 (below average).**
- **St. Joseph, boat: 1 (below average).**
- **Grand Haven plan:** Fish 120-210 ft of water, with lines around 55-110 ft down. Run green, yellow or orange spoons, and try green and white flies deeper.

## Why

- **Grand Haven is the best boat bet:** The Sept 14 Grand Haven report rated boat salmon fishing good, with spoons and flies working in 120-210 ft of water (Grand Haven, 2022-09-14).
- **South Haven is the backup:** Its boat fishing was average on Sept 14 and good on Sept 7, though the Sept 14 report noted anglers "when they could get out" (South Haven, 2022-09-14 and 2022-09-07).
- **Muskegon and St. Joseph ranked lower:** Their most recent boat reports were below average (Muskegon, 2022-09-14; St. Joseph, 2022-09-14).
- **Piers are a poor choice in both recent weeks:** The Grand Haven and Muskegon pier reports were slow (Grand Haven, 2022-09-14 and 2022-09-07; Muskegon, 2022-09-07).

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is Sept 14, six days old)
- Grand Haven, 2022-09-14, boat: quality 3 (good). Water 120-210 ft, fish 55-110 ft down. "Spoons in green, yellow and orange produced good numbers of salmon. … Green and white flies worked well deeper in the water column."
- South Haven, 2022-09-14, boat: quality 2 (average). "Boat anglers targeting salmon had decent fishing when they could get out." The best water was around 110 ft, with spoons catching most fish. Those species entries were not rated.
- Muskegon, 2022-09-14, boat: quality 1 (below average). Water 100-200 ft, fish 55-100 ft down. Green and orange spoons and green flies worked.
- St. Joseph, 2022-09-14, boat: quality 1 (below average). "A couple of boats fishing the pier heads and caught a couple of coho and Chinook."
- The Sept 7 reports were similar: Grand Haven boats were average, South Haven boats were good (quality 3, fish in 110-120 ft and "some good fish caught deeper also"), Muskegon boats were average, and St. Joseph boats were below average.

**Past seasons**
- The similar-weeks search, matching this week's buoy temperature, returned only the 2022 reports above. It found no earlier-season matches, so I have no past-season comparison to add.

**Conditions now**
- The tool returned a summary for the week before Sept 20, not live data. Buoy surface water was about 70-71 F at all four ports, with little change over the week (St. Joseph 45026: 70 F, -1 F; South Haven 45168: 71 F, +0 F; Grand Haven and Muskegon 45029: 71 F, -0 F). That is close to the 72-73 F of the Sept 7 and Sept 14 reports.
- I did not get a modeled cold-layer depth or a wind forecast, so I can't say where the 55 F water sits this week or whether wind will allow boats out.

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old, and fall conditions change quickly. Treat these ratings as expectations from recent reports, not a forecast for the weekend.
- I have no wind forecast. Check the marine forecast before heading out, since South Haven's report hints that wind can keep boats off the water.
- The conditions data is a backtest summary, not live buoy readings, so the water temperatures above are from the week before Sept 20.
- The ratings are my estimates from two recent weeks of reports. Grand Haven's 3 rests on a single good report.

## Sources

- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph DNR bulletin, Sept 14 2022: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32cff90
- DNR bulletin, Sept 7 2022: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32bbcf0
- DNR bulletin, Aug 24 2022: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3298204
